You are implementing build task 1 (repo setup only) for LectorIA-meta, a public repo for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (building period started 2026-10-27). Owner: Martín Madrid Wagner (GitHub martinmw13). Work in the current workspace. Do NOT run git commit, git push, or change git config other than what `npm run prepare` does. Do NOT create any Next.js scaffold, app/, core/, components/, tsconfig, next.config or application code. This task is ONLY repo hygiene, docs, and git hooks. The architecture will be reviewed before app code exists.

Load and follow these project skills: `ponytail` (full level, the default), `unslop` (apply it to every prose file you write), `typescript-best-practices` is not needed (no TS yet). Skills already vendored in `.agents/skills/` (pstack by Lauren Tan, MIT, from github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack at commit 9e88dad; ponytail by DietrichGebert, MIT, github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail at commit 09c434a). Do not edit anything under `.agents/skills/`.

Project context (for the docs): Lectoria is an e-reader that plays orchestral music matched to the emotion of each scene of a public-domain book (text is divided into scenes, not paragraphs or chapters). Live "Picture this" (select a passage, popup, Muse Image illustrates it), live "Picture scene", skip/change track, and a new spoiler-free companion chat in a side panel with the book centered. Demo book: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (Gutenberg #55). Planned stack (NOT built in this task): Next.js App Router + TypeScript on Vercel, shared `core/` module, offline pipeline as Node TS scripts, Python only in `modal/` (Muse Glimmer on Modal), Jev by TypeSafe for emotion classification, Meta API (api.meta.ai/v1, Muse Spark, Muse Image) with BYOK, Upstash Redis for quotas. The earlier March prototype is github.com/martinmw13/lectoria; it is inspiration only and no code is copied.

Create exactly these files:

1. `package.json`: name `lectoria-meta`, private true, type module, `engines.node` ">=20.9", scripts: `prepare` = `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, `check:size` = `node scripts/check-file-size.mjs`, `check:secrets` = `node scripts/check-secrets.mjs`, `test:hooks` = `node --test scripts/`. No dependencies at all. Also `.nvmrc` with `22`.

2. `.githooks/pre-commit` (POSIX sh, executable): runs `node scripts/check-file-size.mjs` then secret scanning: if `gitleaks` is on PATH run `gitleaks git --staged --redact --no-banner` (gitleaks v8.19+ syntax), and ALWAYS also run `node scripts/check-secrets.mjs` (the built-in fallback). Exit non-zero if any fails.

3. `scripts/check-file-size.mjs` (plain Node, no deps): Martin's spec, verbatim: "Create a pre-commit hook that prevents files over 5,000 tokens. Tokens = bytes/4. Run only on staged files. Ignore files which are not authored by agents, like lockfiles or codegen. Provide explicit instructions on how to split files in the error message."
   - Staged files only: `git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR -z`. Measure the STAGED blob size (`git cat-file -s :<path>`), not the working-tree file.
   - tokens = Math.ceil(bytes / 4); fail when tokens > 5000.
   - Ignore list (one exported array of patterns, easy to read): lockfiles (package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, bun.lockb, *.lock, uv.lock, poetry.lock), codegen (*.generated.*, *.gen.*, *.d.ts under generated dirs, next-env.d.ts, `generated/`, `__generated__/`), build output (.next/, dist/, out/, coverage/), processed book data (`public/books/`, `data/processed/`, `pipeline/out/`), all of `public/`, `agent-logs/`, `docs/muse-code-sessions/`, vendored third-party skills `.agents/skills/`, and binary files (detect a NUL byte in the first 8000 bytes of the staged blob, like git does).
   - Error message lists each offending file with bytes and estimated tokens, then explicit split instructions: split by responsibility into small modules (one concern per file, roughly under 300 lines); put shared types in their own file; move fixtures and test data to `fixtures/` or `public/`; for TS/JS create a folder with an `index.ts` that re-exports the pieces so imports stay stable; for docs split by heading into `docs/<topic>/*.md` with a short index; for tests split per behavior; never minify or remove comments to sneak under the limit; and if the file really is generated or third-party, add its pattern to the ignore list in this script and explain why in the commit message.
   - Export a pure function (e.g. `findOversized(entries)` taking `{path, bytes, isBinary}`) so it is testable without git.

4. `scripts/check-secrets.mjs` (plain Node, no deps): scans the staged content (`git show :<path>`) of staged text files, and with `--all` scans every tracked file at HEAD plus `git log -p --all` history. Detect: `jv_live_` keys, OpenAI-style `sk-` keys (`sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}`), Meta API keys if they have a recognizable prefix (treat `LLM|` style tokens and long `Bearer <token>` literals as suspect), GitHub tokens (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `github_pat_`), AWS `AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}`, private key blocks (`-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----`), Upstash/Redis URLs with passwords (`rediss?://[^:\s]+:[^@\s]+@`), and `.env`-style lines `NAME=value` where NAME ends in KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD and the value is 20+ chars with high Shannon entropy (> 3.5 bits/char). Allow `.env.example` lines with empty values or obvious placeholders (`your-`, `changeme`, `<...>`, `xxx`). Refuse to commit any file named `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.*.local` or `*.pem` regardless of content. Never print the secret itself: print file, line number, rule name and a redacted preview (first 4 chars + `…`). Allow an inline `secret-scan:allow` comment on a line for test fixtures. Same ignore list for binaries. Export pure functions for tests.

5. `.githooks/prepare-commit-msg` (POSIX sh, executable): appends the trailer `Co-authored-by: Muse Code (Meta) <muse-code@agents.noreply.invalid>` to every commit message idempotently (use `git interpret-trailers --if-exists doNothing --trailer ...` writing back to the message file, or grep before appending). Skip when `$2` is `merge` or `squash`? No: add it there too, idempotently. Also make it work for `git commit -m`. Keep a single constant for the trailer so it can be changed in one place. (Note: do not use a `users.noreply.github.com` address; a GitHub user named `muse-code` exists and the trailer would credit a stranger.)

6. Tests with `node:test`: `scripts/check-file-size.test.mjs` and `scripts/check-secrets.test.mjs` covering pure functions (oversized file fails, 5000-token file passes, 5001 fails, ignored paths pass, binary passes; each secret rule fires on a fake value built at runtime by string concatenation so the test file itself does not contain a literal secret; `.env.example` placeholders pass; `secret-scan:allow` works). Plus `scripts/hooks.integration.test.mjs` that creates a temp git repo, copies `.githooks/` and `scripts/` in, sets `core.hooksPath`, and proves end to end: (a) committing a 21 KB text file fails with the split instructions in stderr, (b) a small file commits, (c) a 21 KB `package-lock.json` commits, (d) a file containing a fake `jv_live_` key fails, (e) the commit message of a successful commit contains the co-author trailer exactly once even after `git commit --amend --no-edit`. Set user.name/email locally in the temp repo.

7. `.gitignore`: node_modules, .next, out, dist, coverage, .env, .env.local, .env.*.local, *.pem, .vercel, .DS_Store, *.log (but NOT agent-logs/), source epubs (`*.epub`), `data/raw/`.

8. `.env.example` with names only and a one-line comment each, empty values: META_API_KEY, META_MODEL (comment: muse-spark-1.3-contributor in dev, muse-spark-1.3 in public), JEV_API_KEY, JEV_MODEL (pin, e.g. jev-1.14.0), BASETEN_API_KEY, MODAL_TOKEN_ID, MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET, GLIMMER_URL, UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL, UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN, SESSION_SECRET (HMAC key for the anonymous cookie), IP_HASH_SALT, TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY, BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN.

9. `AGENTS.md` (unslopped, sentence-case headings, no emoji). Structure:
   - Top: the ponytail ruleset at FULL level. Copy the always-on ruleset text from `.agents/skills/ponytail/SKILL.md` (the body, minus frontmatter) verbatim, with an attribution line: "Ponytail ruleset by DietrichGebert, MIT, github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail (commit 09c434a).    - "Skills" section: all pstack and ponytail skills live in `.agents/skills/` and Muse Code loads them with `--trust-workspace`. Most pstack skills are user-invocable-only, so prompts must name them. A short skill map table "situation -> skill": designing a task -> `architect`; before writing logic -> `principle-foundational-thinking`, `principle-type-system-discipline`; writing TS -> `typescript-best-practices`; a bug with a cheap test -> `tdd`; debugging -> `principle-fix-root-causes`; finishing a task -> `principle-prove-it-works`; reviewing -> `ponytail-review`, `interrogate`, `blast-radius`; any prose (docs, UI copy, commit messages) -> `unslop`, `technical-writing`; unsure which skill -> read `.agents/skills/poteto-help/SKILL.md`, which maps situations to skills. A rescue by another tool only after that, logged in `RESCUE_LOG.md` with date, task, tool, why Muse got stuck, what changed, and commits, with a `Rescue: <tool>` trailer.    - "Lectoria rules": text is divided into scenes (not paragraphs or chapters); paragraph ids are global like `c12p34`; emotions taxonomy (8): calm, joy, sadness, suspense, mystery, adventure, combat, wonder, plus `unknown` on failure (never fake a fallback emotion); public-domain books only; images follow the book text and W.    - "Writing rules": all docs, UI copy and commit messages are unslopped with the `unslop` skill: no filler, no hype, no emoji headers, no words like seamless, elevate, delve, robust, leverage. Sentence-case headings. Commit messages: imperative subject under 72 chars, body says why.
   - "Design" section (short): minimalist, functional and elegant. No generic AI-template look: no purple or violet anywhere, no gradient blobs, no glassmorphism, no emoji icons, no stock hero sections. Palette from Meta's brand: Meta blue `#0866FF` (hover/pressed `#0064E0`) as the single accent; text near-black `#1C2B33`; surfaces white `#FFFFFF` and soft gray `#F1F4F7`; dark mode with the same accent on a near-black surface (propose `#0B1215` surface, `#E4E6EB` text) ; typography-first reading layout: the book centered with a comfortable measure (about 60 to 70 characters per line), the companion chat in a quiet side panel, generous whitespace, one accent color, subtle motion only (under 200 ms, respects `prefers-reduced-motion`). When the scaffold exists these become CSS custom properties in one tokens file; until then this section is the source of truth.
   - "Hooks": `npm install` (or `npm run prepare`) sets `core.hooksPath` to `.githooks`. What the hooks check and how to run `npm run test:hooks`.

10. `SECURITY.md` (unslopped, short): how to report a vulnerability (GitHub private vulnerability reporting on this repo); what is in place now (env-only secrets, `.env.example`, pre-commit secret scan with gitleaks when installed plus the built-in scanner, GitHub secret scanning and push protection, Dependabot alerts); rules for later tasks (planned, not built yet): BYOK Meta key never stored server-side or in logs, kept only in the browser session (`sessionStorage`) and sent over HTTPS per request in a header; anonymous session cookie signed with HMAC (`SESSION_SECRET`), httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax; IPs stored only as salted hashes (`IP_HASH_SALT`) with daily keys; strict per-person quotas (15 questions and 5 images per day, by hashed IP and anonymous cookie, whichever runs out first) and a global spend cap in Redis; Turnstile once per session; errors never return stack traces or raw exception text; book source files (epub, raw text) are never publicly served, only processed public-domain JSON; security headers and a CSP in `next.config.ts`; input limits (question 500 chars, passage 600 chars) and server-side passage verification.

11. `PRIOR_WORK.md` (unslopped): Lectoria's first version was built in March 2026 at github.com/martinmw13/lectoria (FastAPI + Vite/React). This repo is a from-scratch rewrite started 2026-10-27 for the Meta hackathon. Ideas carried over as ideas only (scenes as the unit, music by emotion with crossfade, Picture this, Picture scene, skip track, BYOK keys only in headers). No code, assets or data were copied. Third-party tools used: pstack (Lauren Tan, MIT) and ponytail (DietrichGebert, MIT), vendored in `.agents/skills/` with their licenses.

12. `BUILT_DURING_HACKATHON.md` (unslopped): a dated log table (date in America/Buenos_Aires, task, what was built, built by). First row: 2026-10-27, task 1 repo setup: hooks, docs, vendored skills; built by Muse Code (muse-spark-1.3-contributor), reviewed by Muse Spark 1.3 Standard. Note the building period dates (2026-10-27 to 2026-11-04 23:00 Buenos Aires).

13. `README.md` (unslopped, short): one paragraph on what Lectoria is, status ("repo setup; app code starts after the architecture review"), how to set up hooks (`npm install` or `npm run prepare`), links to AGENTS.md, SECURITY.md, PRIOR_WORK.md, BUILT_DURING_HACKATHON.md. License line: MIT (create `LICENSE` with MIT, copyright 2026 Martín Madrid Wagner).

14. `.github/dependabot.yml`: npm at `/`, weekly, open-pull-requests-limit 3.

After writing: run `npm run prepare`, `npm run test:hooks`, `node scripts/check-file-size.mjs` and `node scripts/check-secrets.mjs --all` (expect no git HEAD yet; handle a repo with no commits gracefully). Make all tests pass. Every file you author must be under 5000 tokens (20000 bytes). End with a short summary: files created, test results, what you skipped.
